newsitem.title: USA: CME traders expect limit gains in CME hogs Monday.
newsitem.headline: CME traders expect limit gains in CME hogs Monday.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures should post limit gains Monday in reaction to Friday's bullishly construed USDA Hogs and Pigs Report, CME livestock traders said.

The report pegged all hogs on U.S. farms as of December 1 at 96 percent of a year ago, hogs kept for breeding at 97 percent and hogs kept for market at 96 percent, all of which were less than what most analysts expected.
"It is very bullish to the back months of hogs," said one trader, referring to the 97 percent breeding number.
Hogs kept for breeding this past quarter were 97 percent of a year ago, less than all estimates in a pre-report Reuter survey. The estimates ranged from 99.9 to 104.0 percent and averaged 101.6.
USDA reported the total hog supply as of December 1 at 56.171 million head, which was 96 percent of a year ago. Estimates in the Reuter survey ranged from 95 to 101 percent of a year ago.
USDA reported hogs kept for market this past quarter at 96 percent of a year ago versus pre-report trade estimates that ranged from 94 to 99 percent and averaged 97.5.
